quiz_item.scenario_prompt: In Entrepreneurship Requirement 1, what distinguishes an entrepreneur in a market economy from a routine salaried manager?
quiz_item.question: In Entrepreneurship Requirement 1, what distinguishes an entrepreneur in a market economy from a routine salaried manager?
options: A. An entrepreneur is guaranteed a fixed government salary and never faces the possibility of losing invested capital.
B. An entrepreneur avoids innovating or changing product designs and relies on state monopolies to eliminate competitors.

C. An entrepreneur identifies an unmet customer need or market opportunity, organizes resources to create a compelling value proposition, and assumes calculated financial and operational risk to build a venture.
D. An entrepreneur works only in non-profit municipal departments that do not sell goods or services to customers.
choices: A. An entrepreneur is guaranteed a fixed government salary and never faces the possibility of losing invested capital.
B. An entrepreneur avoids innovating or changing product designs and relies on state monopolies to eliminate competitors.

C. An entrepreneur identifies an unmet customer need or market opportunity, organizes resources to create a compelling value proposition, and assumes calculated financial and operational risk to build a venture.
D. An entrepreneur works only in non-profit municipal departments that do not sell goods or services to customers.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. An entrepreneur identifies an unmet customer need or market opportunity, organizes resources to create a compelling value proposition, and assumes calculated financial and operational risk to build a venture.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Entrepreneurs drive innovation and job creation by spotting unmet needs, assembling capital and talent, delivering new value to customers, and taking on calculated business risk.

requirements.lead_text: Create a written business plan for your idea that includes all of the following:
requirements.req_text: Create a written business plan for your idea that includes all of the following: (a) Product or Service (1) Describe the product or service to be offered. (2) Identify goals for your business. (3) Explain how you can make enough of the product or perform the service to meet your goals. (4) Identify and describe the potential liability risks for your product or service. (5) Determine what type of license, if any, you might need in order to sell or make your product or service. (b) Market Analysis (1) Identify the types of people who would buy your product or service. (2) Identify your business's competitors, and describe their strengths and weaknesses. (3) Describe what makes your product or service unique. (c) Financial (1) Determine how much money you will need to start your business, and identify how you will obtain the money. (2) Determine the cost of offering your product or service and the price you will charge in order to make a profit. (3) Describe what will happen with the money you make from the sales of your product or service. (d) Personnel (1) Determine what parts of the business you will handle yourself, and describe your qualifications. (2) Determine whether you will need additional help to operate your business. If you will need help, describe the responsibilities and qualifications needed for the personnel who will fill each role. (e) Promotion and Marketing (1) Describe the methods you will use to promote your business to potential customers. (2) Explain how you will utilize the internet and social media to increase awareness of your product or service. (3) Design a promotional flyer or poster for your product or service.

requirements.description: Create a written business plan for your idea that includes all of the following: (a) Product or Service (1) Describe the product or service to be offered. (2) Identify goals for your business. (3) Explain how you can make enough of the product or perform the service to meet your goals. (4) Identify and describe the potential liability risks for your product or service. (5) Determine what type of license, if any, you might need in order to sell or make your product or service. (b) Market Analysis (1) Identify the types of people who would buy your product or service. (2) Identify your business's competitors, and describe their strengths and weaknesses. (3) Describe what makes your product or service unique. (c) Financial (1) Determine how much money you will need to start your business, and identify how you will obtain the money. (2) Determine the cost of offering your product or service and the price you will charge in order to make a profit. (3) Describe what will happen with the money you make from the sales of your product or service. patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: In Entrepreneurship Requirement 1, what distinguishes an entrepreneur in a market economy from a routine salaried manager?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: In Entrepreneurship Requirement 1, what distinguishes an entrepreneur in a market economy from a routine salaried manager?
options: A. An entrepreneur is guaranteed a fixed government salary and never faces the possibility of losing invested capital.
B. An entrepreneur avoids innovating or changing product designs and relies on state monopolies to eliminate competitors.

C. An entrepreneur identifies an unmet customer need or market opportunity, organizes resources to create a compelling value proposition, and assumes calculated financial and operational risk to build a venture.
D. An entrepreneur works only in non-profit municipal departments that do not sell goods or services to customers.
choices: A. An entrepreneur is guaranteed a fixed government salary and never faces the possibility of losing invested capital.
B. An entrepreneur avoids innovating or changing product designs and relies on state monopolies to eliminate competitors.

C. An entrepreneur identifies an unmet customer need or market opportunity, organizes resources to create a compelling value proposition, and assumes calculated financial and operational risk to build a venture.
D. An entrepreneur works only in non-profit municipal departments that do not sell goods or services to customers.
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. An entrepreneur identifies an unmet customer need or market opportunity, organizes resources to create a compelling value proposition, and assumes calculated financial and operational risk to build a venture.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): Entrepreneurs drive innovation and job creation by spotting unmet needs, assembling capital and talent, delivering new value to customers, and taking on calculated business risk.

patrol_quiz_bank.scenario_prompt: Why is setting specific goals so important when planning and organizing a business?
patrol_quiz_bank.question: Why is setting specific goals so important when planning and organizing a business?
options: A. So you never have to adapt your business plan when market conditions change
B. Because vague goals automatically attract more bank loans than detailed plans
C. Because it is hard to make clear decisions when you only have a general, unfocused goal
D. So you can avoid communicating with employees and customers
choices: A. So you never have to adapt your business plan when market conditions change
B. Because vague goals automatically attract more bank loans than detailed plans
C. Because it is hard to make clear decisions when you only have a general, unfocused goal
D. So you can avoid communicating with employees and customers
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: C. Because it is hard to make clear decisions when you only have a general, unfocused goal
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (C): If you have only a general goal, it is hard to make decisions about how to reach it; setting specific goals guides daily business planning and decision making (p. 10).

options: A. Demanding confidential customer passwords and private bank account numbers
B. Asking only yes-or-no questions about their favorite television shows
C. Pitching your own product for an hour without letting the founder speak
D. Asking how they raised startup capital, built their team, and handled surprises
choices: A. Demanding confidential customer passwords and private bank account numbers
B. Asking only yes-or-no questions about their favorite television shows
C. Pitching your own product for an hour without letting the founder speak
D. Asking how they raised startup capital, built their team, and handled surprises
patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: D. Asking how they raised startup capital, built their team, and handled surprises
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (D): Preparing thoughtful questions about where startup capital came from, what surprises occurred, and how the team was built helps you learn from real-world entrepreneurial experience (p. 40).
